auditor.notes: Fresh subagent that never saw the planning conversation. Inputs used: the plan directory artifacts (input.md, repo-context-snapshot.json, stage-contract.json, candidate-tasks.json, integration-plan.json, dag.json, risk-estimates.json, tasks/T01-T03.json, run-manifest.json), the baseline v1.0 plan-auditor SKILL.md, the baseline glossary.md, the audit schema planning/audit@2, and read-only spot checks of snapshot-listed repo files under evals/probes/repos/p1-notification-retry/. No v1.1 .agents/ artifacts, no other probe runs, no planning chat logs were read.

grounding.notes: All six snapshot files[] entries verified, plus README.md and TASK.md (the snapshot's two unknown_areas entries; opened because the audit instructions explicitly allow them and they ground the raw task and the stdlib claim). Key verifications: (1) tests/test_gateway_observed.py FakeGatewayClient returns 429 with body {'error': 'rate limited'}, headers {'x-gateway': 'edge-3'} (no Retry-After), and the immediate next identical call returns 202 - exactly the A-429-RETRYABLE facts and T01 AT1's four observed values. (2) app/provider.py docstring documents the 429 unknowns T01 cites; ProviderClient.calls exists and FakeGatewayClient appends to it, so E1 call-counting is feasible with the established pattern. (3) app/notify.py record builder matches C2 keys exactly with attempts always 1 today; header comment 'No retry today: first non-2xx -> failed' matches the style constraint; store.put confirms T02's one-put-per-call constraint. (4) tests/test_notify.py assertions (sent/attempts==1 on first-try success; failed/error 'boom' for always-500 client; exactly 1 record) remain compatible with the retry design, so A5 (existing suite green and unmodified) is achievable - the always-500 test asserts only status and error, not attempts or call count. (5) app/api.py handlers call send_notification with the unchanged signature, so 'public handlers stay untouched' holds. (6) README.md confirms Python 3.11, stdlib only, plain unittest (grounds A-NO-NEW-DEPS and the 'repo has no pytest' claim) and treats ProviderClient.send as frozen; TASK.md matches input.md verbatim. No repo movement: content and structure match the snapshot, no AUDIT_SNAPSHOT_MISMATCH condition.

checks_performed: deterministic_lint: ran the v1.0 plan-check.py lint from working dir D:\AI_Coworking\skill-build\planning with schemas from evals/probes/baseline-v1.0/schemas/planning; exit 1; 1 BLOCKER + 0 MAJOR + 22 MINOR; all 23 carried over as findings F01-F23 with the same severity.

scope_creep: compared in_scope/out_of_scope against input.md - every in-scope item (retry loop, 429 handling, the verification task, unit tests, attempts 1..3) traces to the task text; the attempts field already exists in the record (always 1 in app/notify.py today, verified by spot check) so making it reflect real call counts is a consequence of the retry, not B-class creep; product items 2 (bulk-send) and 3 (retry storm) are out-of-scoped with reasons, item 1 (429 unknown) is in scope as T01.

insufficient_non_goals: non-goals in all three packages name the tempting work concretely (app/provider.py frozen, app/db.py, app/api.py, bulk-send, storm mitigation, real time.sleep in tests, new third-party deps); stage out_of_scope carries reasons; no vague 'no refactoring' without a named temptation.

late_contract_freeze: C1/C2/C3 are all frozen:true in stage-contract.json; the parallel consumer T01 (of C1 and C3, owner T02) runs against the frozen inlined specs, and the FALSIFIED path is routed through C1's unfreeze_rule to request_contract_revision at the T03 gate; dag.json unlock_contracts documents the parallelism rationale; the cost of a FALSIFIED verdict (redone 429 branch) is explicitly acknowledged in T02 failure_cases[2] as the accepted cost of the parallel design.

hidden_dependency: carried over the lint case T01 context file app/notify.py -> app/db.py undeclared (F01, verified against snapshot imports); additionally found T02 declaring 'T01 verification decision' as an input while the DAG has no T01->T02 edge and T02 allowed_dependencies is empty (F24); T02 and T03 otherwise read only declared files (T03's allowed_dependencies cover the T01 doc and T02 outputs; its direct file reads are in required_context).

fake_serialization: both DAG edges (T01->T03, T02->T03) are type=verification with substantive reasons (E1-E3 gates verify both leaves); fake_serialization_removed is non-empty and its rationale for rejecting the naive T01->T02 'verify then implement' edge (frozen C1/C3, gate-enforced verdict) survives the 4-type test.

ownership_collision: the only parallel group {T01, T02} has disjoint owned paths (docs/429-behavior-verification.md vs app/notify.py + tests/test_retry.py); T03 runs alone in its group; T03's owns_fixes_for [T01, T02] is an ordered integration-fix right, not an unordered overlap; dag.json collisions_handled agrees.

oversized_leaf: T01 = S, 3 context files, one doc output; T02 = M, 2 layers, 3 contracts, 5 files, P80 75-90 min inside the 90-min stage budget; T03 = M, one test file plus the full-suite gate (e2e_closure with final_acceptance merged, documented in merged_kinds). No leaf crosses >= 5 layers or enumerates phase-like sub-deliverables.

broad_context_loading: T02's 5 context files are all necessary (owned file, frozen boundary it wraps, store it writes through, the two suites A5 requires green); T03's 7 files are all needed by gates E1-E3 and the verdict; T01's third file (app/notify.py) is judged in F01 as not required for the 429 verdict closure.

hidden_integration_work: seams S1 and S2 are both covered_by T03 (gate G1, acceptance A5); E1-E3 include failure scenarios (429 exhaustion -> failed, intermediate record write -> E2 fails, regression of existing tests -> E3 fails); checked omitted_kinds against the snapshot: contract_consistency is justified (E1-E3 exercise all three contracts end to end; C3 untouched - no task owns app/provider.py) and the seam_integration omission is legitimate under the new-wiring rule (spot-checked: only production change is inside existing T02-owned app/notify.py; new files are the doc in a new docs/ dir and test files), but the evidence wording misstates the snapshot (F25).

nondeterministic_acceptance: carried over all 22 lint marker findings (F02-F23); semantically confirmed each criterion is third-party judgeable via its sibling evidence field (named tests/commands) or a doc read with concrete values; no phrase-free vagueness (no 'fast enough' style wording) found; F04 and F07 are the most worth restating.

lack_of_local_recoverability: T01 failure leaves T02 proceedable per the DAG and the T03 gate catches a missing or FALSIFIED verdict; T02 failure invalidates only T02 and T03; T03 failure invalidates only T03; every package has checkpoint_required true; no parallel task owns a path another task needs, and no integration task is gated behind more than the subset that produces its inputs (T01 doc + T02 outputs).
replan_only_by_append: allowed_replan = [split, reorder, defer, replace_route, request_contract_revision] includes shrink/reshape paths (defer, replace_route, split) - not reduced to scope growth.

communication_overhead: all three packages inline the consumed contracts with full spec text and source_hash (executor never needs stage-contract.json); T03's pointer to integration-plan.json for gate text is duplicative because its AT1-AT3 restate the E1-E3 scenarios; no unnecessary reviewer hops or duplicated checkpoint content.

grounding / repo movement: read-only spot checks of the eight snapshot-listed files (see grounding block) found no content or structure drift versus the snapshot; every repo-facing plan claim checked was confirmed (see grounding notes); no AUDIT_SNAPSHOT_MISMATCH condition.

findings.evidence: tasks/T02.json inputs[0] = 'T01 verification decision (must be CONFIRMED; if FALSIFIED, stop and replan via request_contract_revision)' and T02.json allowed_dependencies = [], but dag.json has no T01->T02 edge (parallel_groups = [[T01,T02],[T03]], edges only T01->T03 and T02->T03). The same stale 'T02 consumes T01' view also appears in candidate-tasks.json (T01 downstream_consumers = [T02]) and tasks/T01.json integration_dependency.consumers = [T02, T03], while T02.json failure_cases[2] itself says the FALSIFIED verdict is 'discovered at the T03 integration gate, after this task's code exists'.
findings.suggested_fix: T02's declared input contradicts the DAG it must execute under: a fresh executor reading T02's inputs literally will stall waiting for T01's document (or stop early) while the DAG says proceed in parallel. Rewrite T02 inputs to 'C1 (inlined, frozen) including the retryable-429 branch; T01 verifies A-429-RETRYABLE in parallel - its verdict is enforced at the T03 gate via request_contract_revision, not at T02 start', and remove 'T02' from candidate-tasks T01 downstream_consumers and T01.json integration_dependency.consumers (T03 is the consumer of the doc).

findings.evidence: integration-plan.json omitted_kinds[seam_integration].evidence = ['S1', 'S2', 'repo-context-snapshot.json (no docs/ dir exists; tests/ files all owned by T02)'] - the snapshot lists tests/test_notify.py and tests/test_gateway_observed.py as pre-existing repo files owned by no task (T02 owns only tests/test_retry.py), so 'tests/ files all owned by T02' is false as stated.
